author: Rahul kp
title: Operating vs
simple_words: Operating leverage magnifies sales into EBIT. Financial leverage magnifies EBIT into EPS.

definitions.meaning: Effect of ==fixed operating costs== on EBIT. A small change in sales causes a larger % change in EBIT.
Effect of ==fixed financial costs== (interest) on EPS. A small change in EBIT causes a larger % change in EPS.

key_points: DOL comes from fixed operating costs such as rent and depreciation.
DFL comes from debt and fixed financial charges such as interest.
With no fixed operating cost, DOL is 1. With no interest, DFL is 1.
!!Combined leverage = DOL × DFL!! shows total risk from sales to EPS.

formulas.name: Degree of Operating Leverage
formulas.legend: Contribution = Sales − Variable cost. EBIT = Contribution − Fixed operating cost.

formulas.name: Degree of Financial Leverage
formulas.legend: EBT = Earnings before tax. Interest = fixed interest on debt. No preference dividend assumed.

formulas.name: Degree of Combined Leverage
formulas.legend: DCL = % change in EPS ÷ % change in Sales.

insight.punchline: Same fixed cost idea, two spots!
insight.text: Fixed cost above EBIT gives operating leverage; fixed cost below EBIT gives financial leverage.

memory_trick.explanation: Operating costs sit Over the EBIT line (Sales to EBIT). Interest Falls below it (EBIT to EPS). DCL multiplies both.

steps: Deduct fixed cost to get EBIT
DFL = EBIT ÷ EBT; DCL = DOL × DFL
exam_tip: If a question gives fixed cost as a % of EBIT, DOL = (EBIT + Fixed cost) ÷ EBIT. Work it out from this.

doubt.question: Does higher leverage always mean higher profit?
doubt.answer: No. It magnifies both gains and losses. When sales or EBIT fall, EBIT or EPS falls faster, so risk rises.

mistakes_hook: check the numerator, check the base

mistakes.right: DOL = Contribution ÷ EBIT. Contribution is on top.
DFL = EBIT ÷ (EBIT − Interest). Interest is deducted to get EBT.
DCL = DOL × DFL. Combined leverage is a product, not a sum.
